statements.justification: The four values match, but the 'SALL1→SALL4→SOX2→NANOG wave' is not in time order: NANOG peaks first (+0.06, 9mo), SALL4 last (+0.08, 3mo). Shifts of 0.05-0.08 in genes barely expressed in blood look like noise. The cited paper shows OCT4/NANOG/SOX2 rising after 4-7 days of culture, not in circulating leukocytes.

Values match (ACOT4 relevant, -0.07 to -0.12). But the mechanism is reversed: ACOTs turn acyl-CoA into free fatty acid, so less ACOT4 predicts fewer, not more, free fatty acids. The fatty-acid 'rise' is only mid-window (6mo); at 12mo, with ACOT4 down, oleate is -0.30.
statements.in_paper_where: Results, 'Enrichment and partial correlation analysis' and Fig. 3b: fatty acids up in cases (no ACOT mentioned).

statements.justification: ACOT2 values match, but +0.04 at one window is noise level, and it is not the only ACOT with a 9mo bump (ACOT9 +0.06, ACOT6 +0.04). Fatty acids peak at 6mo, when ACOT2 is -0.01. The cited mouse work says Acot2 raises fatty-acid oxidation; S2 explains the same rise by the opposite mechanism.
statements.in_paper_where: Results, 'Enrichment and partial correlation analysis' and Fig. 3b: fatty acids up in cases (no ACOT mentioned).

statements.justification: Values and relevance flags match (HDAC10 is the only relevant HDAC). But calling the HDAC changes 'baseline differences rather than a coordinated response' misreads the design: 12mo is a case-control difference, the paper's most predictive window. The aged-skin citation (HDAC10 and HDAC11 both down) neither supports that nor fits HDAC11 up, HDAC10 down here.

HDAC11 +0.17 at 12mo, not relevant: correct. The cited HDAC11-represses-IL-10 link is sound and would fit the paper's IL10-down finding (IL10 negative in all windows here). But 'a baseline difference, not a response' misreads the design: 12mo is a case-control difference, the paper's most predictive window.
statements.in_paper_where: Results, 'TNFα activation by ROS accumulation...': IL10 and TGFβ down, higher APC activity (Fig. 6); HDAC11 not mentioned.

statements.justification: HDAC8 -0.13 at 12mo, not relevant: correct, and the HEK293 RIG-I citation is accurate. But the 12mo case-control value is again dismissed as 'baseline', and 'consistent with the pre-seroconversion window' says nothing; if anything, a stronger, not weaker, interferon signature is reported before islet autoimmunity.

APOC3 values match (relevant, +0.05 at 3mo). The citation is about coronary calcium and insulin resistance in adults with established type 1 diabetes, not about risk of the disease or pre-autoimmunity, so the 'thus' does not follow. Higher APOC3 would raise triglycerides, yet triglycerides are lower in cases at every window.
statements.in_paper_where: Abstract; Results, 'Lipid metabolism irregularities...' (lipid abnormalities before IA; APOC3 not mentioned).

statements.justification: All values and flags match. APOA1 (LCAT's activator), LCAT and its substrate phosphatidylcholine all down, with cholesteryl esters slightly lower in cases (-0.02 to -0.04), make reduced HDL cholesterol esterification a fair hypothesis extending the paper's APOA1/HDL discussion. Caveats: LCAT is a liver enzyme; 'transient' fits LCAT only.
statements.in_paper_where: Results, 'Lipid metabolism irregularities...': APOA1 down, structural lipids down, HDL phospholipid hydrolysis; Figs 3b, 5. LCAT not mentioned.

statements.justification: Values match: BTD (relevant) near zero until +0.14 at 0mo, close to the top 1% of gene differences; HLCS not relevant and flat. Citations correctly describe the biotin cycle and biotin's effect on dendritic cells, and the statement admits the direction is unknown. Cautious and data-grounded, but thin; not in the paper.

KARS values match (relevant). The 'late' framing is selective: 12mo (+0.09) equals 3mo (+0.10). LysRS's non-canonical immune role is real, though cited from a background sentence of a leukodystrophy abstract. As a hedged link to the paper's late immune activation it is acceptable, but weak.

Values match, but C1QB and C1QC are not relevant (unstated), while C1QA, also not relevant, is set aside as 'up from baseline, a sustained shift rather than a response'. That misreads the design: 12mo is a case-control difference. All three co-regulated C1q chains are up at 0mo (+0.08, +0.11, +0.06).

Values and flags match, but GALR3 shifts of +0.01 to +0.04 in a neural receptor barely expressed in blood are noise level. 'Pro-inflammatory in immune settings' rests on one mouse psoriasis model; the rat thymocyte paper shows apoptosis. A ligand dip does not support 'tonic' signalling, and nothing links to islet autoimmunity.

Values match: CARD6 relevant, +0.11 and +0.16 early (also +0.13 at 3mo); RIPK2 not relevant, though -0.08 to +0.08 is not quite flat. The citation does show CARD6 binding NOD1 and RIPK2 and suppressing their NF-κB signalling. A hedged, reasonable innate-immune link the paper did not make.

The 'APC2' row is another gene (APC regulator of WNT signalling 2); the real APOC2 row is not relevant and is -0.02 at 6mo, +0.10 at 9mo. 'Indicates reduced LPL-mediated clearance' is stated as fact from blood mRNA and predicts higher triglycerides, yet triglycerides are lower in cases at every window.

overall.comment: Every quoted value matches the uploaded files, and S8 (APOA1-LCAT-phosphatidylcholine) touches the paper's lipid conclusion. But the walk drifts through generic neighbourhoods (pluripotency, histones, galanin), repeatedly dismisses 12-month case-control differences as 'baseline' although that is the paper's most predictive window, gives contradictory fatty-acid mechanisms (S2 vs S3) and maps APC2 onto APOC2. It does not reach the paper's ROS/energy-metabolism or immune-activation conclusions.
